Web · Resources

Guide Markdown how-to conventions

Guides now read as how-tos: copyable paths, screenshots between numbered steps, shortcut callouts that carry their payload, and side-by-side before/after photos. Duplicate page titles and task-list checkboxes are gone.

After only

No trustworthy before PNG for this second convention pass. Captures are Cursor IDE Chromium at ~1372×1160 CSS pixels (1× PNGs), ADMIN Erik Role, dark appearance, authenticated local Preview at 127.0.0.1:3000 on 2026-09-19. The Next.js 1-issue overlay is HMR chrome, not product UI.

What changed, and why

Copyable paths and rename strings

Was

Server paths and rename templates lived in inline code or a terminal-styled fence, so people retyped them.

Now

A fenced ```copy / ```path block renders as a one-tap copy control on web and iOS. The editor toolbar inserts it with Copyable.

Screenshots sit between steps

Was

Images nested inside list items, or H3s used as fake step numbers, so badges and numbering broke.

Now

Figures are their own block. A following 2. / 3. continues the sequence through the list start value and CSS counters.

Callouts carry the payload

Was

A Shortcut card sometimes only pointed at a table below, and iOS flattened tables inside quotes.

Now

Shortcut, tip, and warning cards contain the actual shortcuts and recovery copy. Keyboard chips have no plus separators.

How-to page hygiene

Was

Several guides opened with a Markdown h1 that duplicated the page title. Video Captioning used GFM task lists. Photo Mechanic was not typed How-to.

Now

A matching lead h1 is stripped. Task lists are ordinary bullets. Photo Mechanic is How-to. How-to and Media Drive templates follow the same conventions.

Before/after photos

Was

Paired stills stacked as separate figures with Pre/Post headings.

Now

Two images in one paragraph lay out as a two-column pair. Color Correction 101 has four verified pairs.
